Accolade

AK-uh-layd -- three syllables, stress on the first syllable, AK. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Accolade is an honor or award granted to someone in recognition of an achievement.

Having the new wing named after her was an accolade the librarian never expected.

Worked Example

At the end-of-season banquet, the swim coach calls one name last. The team's quietest swimmer walks up to receive the Captain's Cup -- and the whole room rises to its feet.

The Cup is an accolade: a specific honor or piece of praise given in recognition of what someone has done. An accolade is countable -- you can collect accolades the way you collect trophies -- and each one marks a particular achievement.

How Accolade Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

honor

honor: public recognition of achievement or worth

tribute

tribute: an act or gift that shows deep respect

distinction

distinction: a mark of special recognition or excellence

Antonyms

insult

insult: a remark or act meant to belittle someone

rebuke

rebuke: a sharp statement of disapproval

How Strong Is It? — honor → accolade → tribute

honor vs. accolade

honor vs. accolade: Honor is the broad, weaker term -- almost any recognition counts as an honor -- while an accolade is a specific, named piece of praise or an award actually handed to you.

tribute vs. accolade

tribute vs. accolade: Tribute is the strongest of the three: an accolade recognizes an achievement, but a tribute honors the whole person, often publicly and at length -- a plaque is an accolade; an evening of speeches is a tribute.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ac-

prefix — ac-: to, toward (Latin ad-)

root — col-

root — col-: neck (Latin collum)

suffix — -ade

suffix — -ade: act or result of (French -ade)

Put it together

Put it together: Accolade comes from French accolade, 'an embrace around the neck' -- ad- ('to') plus collum ('neck'). When a knight was dubbed, he received a ceremonial embrace or a tap on the shoulders; that gesture of conferring honor became the word for the honor itself.

Root Check

Word Choice

Accolade is countable and often plural: the film earned countless accolades. Keep it apart from this unit's acclaim, which is the roar of public praise itself -- acclaim is the applause; an accolade is the trophy. You receive an accolade; you enjoy acclaim.
